chunk_findings.detail: A run that recorded a positive sub-second wait is silently dropped from gate status. `_queued_notes` uses `w >= 1`, so given evidence `waited_s=0.5` and `elapsed_s=10.0`, the function returns no `queued` note even though the run “waited at all” (the docstring’s own criterion) and the change’s intent is to show wait in gate status. `runner._waited` can produce such values, e.g. `p.waited_s = 0.5`, so this is reachable, not synthetic. The status line should be emitted for any positive recorded wait, or the threshold should be justified in the code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py:286

chunk_findings.detail: `wait_line` formats the wait with `:g`, which switches to scientific notation for values at or above 1e6. For example, `wait_line(1000000.0)` returns `"ddflow-suite-wait 1e+06"`, but `_WAIT_LINE` only accepts `[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?`, so `parse_wait()` on that exact line returns `None`. A full-suite run queued for ~11.6 days is then silently recorded as having no wait, contradicting the intent that a recorded wait is readable. Use a fixed notation for `wait_line` or make `_WAIT_LINE` accept exponent notation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_marker.py wait_line / parse_wait

chunk_findings.detail: For a non-`ci` gate, `waited_s` is produced solely from the runner’s admission-slot wait (`_waited` sets `lock=None` because `gdef.id != "ci"`), but `_queued_notes` still renders `"queued 30s for the host lock"`. A gate that waited only for a worker admission slot is reported as waiting for the host suite lock, which is not the recorded wait; the runner comment itself says `waited_s` covers "the host suite lock or an admission slot". Concrete example: gate `test` with `p.waited_s=30` and no `ci` output produces evidence `waited_s=30.0` and status `test -- queued 30s for the host lock`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py:_queued_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `w >= 1` suppresses status notes for recorded, non-zero waits under one second. For example, evidence `waited_s=0.5` (produced by `_waited` from a 0.5s admission-slot wait) leaves `queued` empty, so `ddflow gate status` reports no wait even though the run "waited at all" and the wait is present in facts/metrics. This makes the status view inconsistent with the recorded `waited_s` evidence for sub-second waits.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py:_queued_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The new render branch formats `r['wait_max_s']`, but `ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py` populates the `wait_*` keys by spreading the existing `stat()` result. The existing `stat()` output was consumed as `n`, `p50_s`, and `p90_s` (the original gate_time row reads only those), and this change does not add a `max_s` key anywhere. Given any metrics render where a gate has at least one recorded `waited_s` (`wait_n > 0`), `r['wait_max_s']` is absent, so rendering raises `KeyError: 'wait_max_s'` instead of showing the new wait metric.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:47 (wait_max_s indexing)

chunk_findings.detail: The negative test does not fully guard the stated requirement that old logs without `waited_s` report `None`, never zero. It only checks `row["wait_p50_s"] is None` for `_log([None])`. The same row model also carries `wait_max_s` (used at line 62), but the implementation could compute e.g. `wait_max_s` as `0.0` when there are no wait samples and this test would still pass, violating the intent. It should assert every reported `wait_*` metric is `None` when `wait_n == 0` (and that the fact outcome has `waited_s is None`).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_lock_wait.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: `_waited` rounds `p.waited_s` to one decimal before deciding whether a wait happened. Given `p.waited_s=0.04` for a non-`ci` gate, `slot` becomes `0.0`; since `lock is None` and `not slot` is true, the function returns `None`, and no `waited_s` evidence is recorded even though the run waited for an admission slot. This contradicts the new behavior (“runner adds slot wait”, and the evidence comment “absent when the run waited for nothing it can name”). The positivity check should be made on the unrounded `p.waited_s`, then only the final sum should be rounded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:_waited (line 89)

chunk_findings.detail: The new render branch accesses `r['wait_max_s']`, but `summary.py` builds the `wait_*` keys by prefixing every key returned by the existing `stat` helper used for gate durations. `stat` returns only `n`, `p50_s`, and `p90_s` (the old renderer only consumed those two percentiles), so no `wait_max_s` key exists. A gate with a recorded `waited_s` sample (e.g. one outcome with `waited_s=2.0`) produces a `gate_time` row with `wait_n=1`, enters the branch, and raises `KeyError: 'wait_max_s'` before metrics can render.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/render.py:49

chunk_findings.detail: The new metrics line labels every `waited_s` sample as `queued for the lock`, but `waited_s` is defined in `ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py` as time spent queued for “the host suite lock or an admission slot.” A non-`ci` gate that only waited for a worker admission slot (e.g. gate `test` with `waited_s=30` and no CI host-suite lock wait) is rendered as `(queued for the lock: n=1 p50 30s max 30s)`, misreporting the kind of wait in `ddflow metrics`. The same kind of mislabel was already confirmed and fixed in `outcomes._queued_notes`, but this new metrics render surface still presents an admission-slot wait as a lock wait.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous LOW still holds in the producer path, so the cited runner-only test does not answer it. `waited = round(time.monotonic() - queued_at, 1)` turns a real 0.04 s suite-lock wait into `0.0`; `ci_marker.wait_line` then renders even a raw 0.04 as `ddflow-suite-wait 0.0`, and `parse_wait` returns `0.0`. A full-suite `ci run` that actually queued 0.04 s therefore records `waited_s=0.0`, so the nonzero wait is lost before the runner can decide it happened.

chunk_findings.detail: A non-ci gate whose `CommandRun.waited_s` is `0.04` now avoids the previous `None` return, but `_waited` still does `round((lock or 0.0) + slot, 1)`, so the stored evidence is `waited_s: 0.0`. `outcomes._queued_notes` requires `w > 0`, so this run’s wait is omitted from gate status, and anything downstream that treats a positive `waited_s` as “did wait” will see a false zero. The run did wait for an admission slot, so the stored value should preserve that the wait was positive (store the unrounded value or round away from zero for this threshold), not round `0.04` to `0.0`.

chunk_findings.detail: A real sub-millisecond wait still collapses to zero: for a non-ci gate with `CommandRun(waited_s=0.0004)`, `slot` is `0.0004`, so `lock is None and not slot` is `False` and `_waited` returns `round(0.0004, 3) == 0.0`. The run did wait 0.4 ms, but `outcomes._queued_notes` requires `w > 0`, so this positive wait is omitted from gate status/metrics. chunk_findings.detail: The new tests never exercise the real recording path. `_log` hand-inserts `waited_s` into `gate.passed` evidence, and the only runner check calls `R._waited(...)` in isolation. A runner implementation that computes `_waited` but never writes it into the passed evidence would still pass this file: for a `unit_tests` gate with `CommandRun(..., waited_s=3.2)`, `_waited` returns `3.2`, while the recorded log event still lacks `waited_s`, defeating the change's requirement to record the wait as evidence.

chunk_findings.detail: `parse_wait` scans the whole log and returns the *last* line matching the fixed `ddflow-suite-wait ` sentinel, with no distinction between the outer `ci run` wait line and identical-looking text emitted later by the command under test (or by a nested `ddflow ci run`). Given an output string such as `"ddflow-suite-wait 0.123456\nprintf 'ddflow-suite-wait 10.000000'\n"`, `parse_wait` returns `10.0`, so the gate records a false wait that overwrites the real one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_marker.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: `waited = round(time.monotonic() - queued_at, 6)` still collapses any positive wait below 0.5 microseconds to `0.0`: for a full-suite run that queued `0.0000004` seconds, `res.waited_s` is stored as `0.0` and `ci_marker.wait_line` prints `ddflow-suite-wait 0.000000`, so a real wait is recorded as zero rather than preserved. This is the same class as the previously fixed `0.0004` case, just below the new 6-decimal cutoff; a test probing `0.04` does not cover it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_mins` renders any positive wait under 0.05 seconds as `"0.0s"` because it uses `f"{seconds:.1f}s"` for values below 10. `_queued_notes` then produces a gate status line such as `queued 0.0s before it ran`. For the same `CommandRun(waited_s=0.04)` case the new test name says is “still a recorded wait”, the stored evidence is positive, but the user-facing gate status says the run queued zero seconds. That contradicts the change intent to show the wait in gate status.
